study_label.what: Heroes of Faith: Brother Andrew and his Bible smuggling work

evidence.text: Well, over the coming months, I'm not quite sure how long it will take, we're going to look at a number of people who have loved Jesus and in some way have made a difference for Jesus. we're going to call these people heroes of faith and i think we've got a slide coming up on the screen just to remind us of the title of the series heroes of faith some of the heroes will be women some will be men some will be people from a long way back in history. Others will still be alive. Some we will know, some we may not know. They may be missionaries or pastors or evangelists. They may be poets and writers. They may be people who have done all kinds of things for Jesus. Well, today we're going to look at a man who has become known as Brother Andrew. Brother Andrew. I think we've got a picture of him up the front. Two pictures of him, actually. One when he was younger. One when he was a bit older. I think he's still alive today. As far as I know, he's still alive. He was born in 1928. Well, as many of you will probably know, It's difficult to be a Christian in some countries around the world today. It's difficult for Christians to meet. It's difficult for them to read their Bibles and to study their Bibles together. In some countries, you're not supposed to have a Bible. Certainly you can't go out to a shop and buy a Bible. Well, many years ago, Brother Andrew was really concerned about this. And he wanted to serve Jesus and Christians in persecuted countries by getting to them Bibles. You know, we almost take it for granted, don't we, that we 've got a Bible in our hands. I've got lots of Bibles sitting on my shelves at home. Brother Andrew was concerned. And he resolved that he would do everything possible to get Bibles into countries where soldiers and policemen and border guards would do their utmost in various countries to try to stop him. And I think we've got a picture there of a soldier at the border. This is the kind of person that would have wanted to stop Brother Andrew. But he was determined. And I don't know whether you've read his story, but he used many different cars full of Bibles, I was going to say stacked with Bibles, to take Bibles to these various countries. Now obviously it was a dangerous thing for him to do. he could have got stopped and found himself in a lot of trouble but but wonderfully you know the lord watched over andrew as well as the bibles and somehow the soldiers or the guards or the police or whoever they were never saw the bibles isn 't that wonderful and so if we look at the last picture, we see that many Christians have the joy of not only receiving a Bible, but being able to study the Bible on their own or with other Christians. It's a wonderful thing, isn't it, to have the Bible, to be able to read God 's word to us, because that is what it is and to discover in the bible about jesus and the way of salvation we truly are a privileged people but we can thank god today for people like brother andrew who have risked their well-being in order to get bibles to people who really need them well in the light of that shall Shall we pray for the persecuted church? And let's pray as well for the translation of Bibles into different languages so that people who desire to read the Bible are able to read it for themselves. Let's pray. Lord, we thank you that throughout the history of the Christian church that you have burdened many individuals to carry out tasks for your glory and for the well-being of your church. And we thank you for the burden that you gave to Brother Andrew all those years ago. And we thank you for the dangerous missions, as it were, that he has undertaken over the years, trying to smuggle Bibles into countries where it's prohibited. Thank you for his courage. Thank you, Lord, for his success. We realize that the courage was God-given and that success was God-given. And we praise you and give you all the glory, therefore. We pray for those who are still trying to get Bibles into countries where the authorities come down very hard on Christians and their faith. Pray that you would grant them success. We pray for those who are engaged in the work of Bible translation. We've had the Bible in English now for many, many years and we're so thankful for that. especially in view of the fact that there were those who suffered greatly in order to make this happen at the beginning, we do ask that you would help them to produce really good Bible translations. We pray that you would grant them success in their work, So that those people groups might be able to read and study the Bible in their own language. Thank you that you gift and equip people to understand the Hebrew and the Greek, as well as other foreign languages, so that they are able to do this vital work. Please add your blessing, we pray, and we ask these things in Jesus' name. Amen.

study_label.what: Gladys Aylward biography teaching availability to Jesus

evidence.text: Good morning to look at some of the great heroes of faith I'll mention the name that we're going to be thinking about this morning in just a moment but first I'd like to show you three things and I want you to tell me what it is that you think these three things have in common may not be that easy but let's see Let's see how we go. I don't know whether you can see that. On the TV screen. Or at the back of the church. But it's a pencil. It's a pencil. The next item is a spoon. A pencil. A spoon. And the other item is a book. And I'll give you a moment just to think about it. But is there anything you think these three things have. In common. In common. In common. Well the answer is this. They're all very ordinary. There's nothing particularly extraordinary about them. They're three very ordinary household items. Well the person that we're going to think about this morning. And her picture will appear on the screen any moment. Is Gladys Aylward. Gladys Aylward. Who was born in 1902. And died in 1970. Two years before I was born. Now Gladys Aylward was a very ordinary person. Is it. Can we have the first picture up. Is that all right. A very ordinary person. She was not particularly clever. In fact there was a time when she tried to learn Chinese. Whilst living in this country. But didn't do very well at all. She was not particularly rich. In fact she came from a very ordinary family. Her father was a postman. And her first job was a housemate. That meant that she spent her days looking after a wealthy person's house. Doing all their cleaning and tidying. And so on and so forth. Gladys was a very ordinary person. But she had a very extraordinary friend. And his name of course. Was Jesus. And Jesus wanted Gladys to go and tell people about him in China. Actually one day Gladys was reading an article in a magazine. And it was all about how the people in China hadn't heard about Jesus. And she really felt convicted. That China was the place that Jesus wanted her to go. The trouble was. None of the missionary organizations would send her. You see they only considered her to be an ordinary person. Not someone worthy of being involved in missionary work. But Gladys was convinced that she should go to China. And so she saved up her money. And she made her own way there. And if we look at the next slide. We can see the journey that she took. Which of course was all across land. Quite a journey. Well although many thought of her to be an ordinary person. With Jesus' help she did some extraordinary things. Let me list some of them. She ran a hotel in the middle of nowhere. And told the travelers all about Jesus. She worked for the government for a while. Tending to people's feet. And while she was looking after their feet. She told people about Jesus. And actually she was a woman that came to look after over 500 children. And we've got a picture of her. With a little Chinese lad. No one else you see was willing to love these children. But Gladys took them under her wings so to speak. And loved them with the love of the Lord Jesus. And of course she told them about the Lord Jesus. And when the war came to China. She kept her children from danger. By walking with them for days and days. Across the mountains. In order that they might avoid the fighting. We've got a picture of that to finish with. There she is in the mountains. With her children. Many people thought that Gladys. That Gladys was too ordinary for missionary work in China. But Jesus didn't. I wonder whether we feel like very ordinary people. There's nothing particularly special or unique or amazing about us. But you know if we make ourselves available to Jesus. Then who knows how Jesus might be willing to use us. So our story this morning. Is all about Gladys. Gladys. Gladys Aylward. And I trust that we'll learn an important lesson. From her life. And story.

study_label.what: Interview reporting children’s ministry at Keswick and Buzz Club

evidence.text: Well, as you know, it's Buzz Club this week. And I'm going to ask Steve, our speaker, for the week, if he'll come out to the front. You've met Steve before. We've heard something of his testimony. So I'm not going to ask him to give that to us again. But I have got a few questions to put to him. So if you want to stand in front of that, it'll pick you up . Steve, first of all, tell us where you and your family have been this week. And what have you been doing? Thank you. Good morning, everyone. It's good to be with you again. The last fortnight, my family and I have been in Keswick in the Lake District. We've been there for a week of receiving teaching at the Keswick Convention. Some of you will have heard of, maybe even visited. And then last week, we were there for a second week. And we were serving, volunteering at the convention. And my wife was helping with the creche there. And I was volunteering with a fours to fives group of children for the week. So it was a huge privilege to be there. As you can imagine, I'm in need of a lot of prayer for energy for the coming week. Not ideal preparation for being with you, but it was a huge encouragement being there. And apparently the convention this year, the three weeks of the convention, had 3,000 young people, teenagers, children, going through the children's and youth work there. So it was a privilege to be part of a great experience. And that was record numbers, wasn't it? Record numbers, yes. Those of you who are interested in the convention, week three, the week we volunteered for, just in the children's category, there were 300 children on the waiting list who couldn't get into the children's work, at least until later on in the week when some people had gone home. So a huge challenge for the convention with a great blessing and encouragement as well. And the children study the same material from the Bible as the adults, don't they? Yes. The week three, the main preacher, Vaughan Roberts, was, is it Roberts? Yeah, Vaughan Roberts. Vaughan Roberts, that's right. He was speaking on Psalms. So even in the threes and fours group, they would teach the same basic material or the same Bible references. In fact, week two when we were there, the adults had Ezek iel. So who was, who was, all credit to those who were applying and teaching Ezekiel to the threes and fours. But I'm sure that was a challenge and a blessing, I'm sure. Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. How old were children at Pesach all the way from age three all the way till, well, there was special work for 19 to 24 year olds. But in terms of 3,000 people or 3,000 young people, I think they go from the age of three or four up to 18. So huge privilege and opportunity. Okay, so from the Lake District to Crockenhill, tell us what you're going to be speaking to the children about this coming week, so that we can pray for you. Yes, please, please do. We'd be much in prayer for you as a church. In the lead look to the week as well, and not just any part time I'd be playing in it, but everyone involved and those who won't be here directly through prayer, crucial that you as a church, praying that the Lord would bring fruit from this week. And we're going to be looking at a number of parables during the mornings and the Thursday evening service, if you like, meeting, under the title, Totally Tremendous Tales of Truth. We all like a bit of alliteration, don't we? So there we are. Monday we're going to be looking at the parable of the wise and foolish builders, under the title, Be Wise. So, challenging the children to not only listen to the words of the Lord Jesus Christ, but to live in accordance with them. Tuesday, be forgiven, the parable of the prodigal or the lost son, the necessity for repentance and faith for even youngsters amongst us. Be amazed, on Wednesday morning, the parable of the hidden treasure and the pearl, trying to see, help the children to see the awesomeness, if you like, of the Lord Jesus Christ, that he's worthy of leaving everything to follow him. And then Thursday morning, the parable of the ten young women or ten virgins, thinking about the return of the Lord Jesus Christ and how we're to live in response to that, as we've been thinking about this morning. Some of the children, you may know some of the children who are coming, you may not. Just for some of the children, I imagine this idea that the Lord Jesus Christ is going to return one day, I'm just totally new to them, from my experience, working in schools. And then Thursday evening, at the final gathering, for adults as well, we're going to be thinking about the parable of the Pharise e and the tax collector, and that idea that you so often hear in society today, that to be a Christian means that you are a good person, that you're morally upright and whatever, rather than from standing from the viewpoint that we all need God's forgiveness, that none of us is good, we need his forgiveness, and we need his transforming work. So that's where we'll be going, God willing. But please continue to pray. I know you've been praying as a church, you will have been praying, continue to pray, pray for fruit, and please pray, particularly as an outsider, but I think even someone who knows the area better, it's hard sometimes to pitch the talks, you'll have some children who haven't got a clue, you might have some who are a bit more familiar with the Bible, and then four-year-olds, eleven-year-olds, very different beasts in many ways, so just pray for wisdom for me for that as well, and a bit of preparation still to do it. So I value prayer as I spend a couple of the afternoons getting where I ought to be. So thank you, very much value your prayers. That's fair enough, if you've been up in Keswick all week.

study_label.what: Report on Abby’s UBM beach mission week

evidence.text: Right, we've got a special offer this week. Not only me from the front, we've got another special guest . Abby's going to join me just for a couple of questions. Thank you, Abby. Where have you been this past week? Past week, I've been in Cornwall in Newquay doing a UBM beach mission. And yeah, we were staying in Newquay Evangelical Church in the building next to it. There were 19 of us. So, yeah. Good. And tell us about what the day involved and what your involvement was. Yeah. So some mornings I went into the town and we did a question of the day and we spoke to the public about their thoughts on it. And then in the afternoon, we did a programme on the beach and we were chatting to people. We were doing lots of games with the kids, chatting to the parents, yeah, things like that. And how were you encouraged by stuff this week? I think I had some very interesting conversations with people. I had a conversation with one man who was a Buddhist and he said that the only way he could reach heaven or his form of heaven was through meditating and he believed that he was a god. But I explained some concepts to him like Jesus coming to die for us and he seemed really open to it. So yeah, conversations like that. So that's one prayer point. Are there any other prayer points from the week? I think it was, I wasn't really sure how to share my faith before. I think it was a really great week, which helped me to realise that I can just say, what do you think about this to people and start a conversation that way. So I think being able to do that more with my friends or just people I meet spontaneously and things like that. So, yeah. Brilliant. Thank you very much. Thank you.
